react_result.final_narrative_text: The eight differentially abundant metabolites converge on a coherent biological-oxidations and xenobiotic-metabolism signal across three independent enrichment paradigms. RaMP ORA identifies REACT:R-HSA-211859 'Biological oxidations' as the top hit (FDR=1.33×10⁻⁴, fold enrichment=124), driven by three input compounds: methimazole (an imidazole-thione drug), L-cysteine (the central sulfur amino acid), and coumarin (a benzopyrone). The same three-metabolite cluster also drives the Reactome 'Phase I – Functionalization of compounds' sub-pathway (R-HSA-211945, FDR=0.0022), which is the biochemical mechanism underlying Phase I xenobiotic metabolism. Mummichog independently nominates the m/z-derived pathway 'Xenobiotics metabolism' (MUMM:xenobiotics_metabolism) as its top hit (p=0.0019, rank 1), with coumarin and catechol as network-neighbor hits. Catechol (pyrocatechol, CHEBI:18135) is a prototypical monooxygenase substrate, and the benzo[a]pyrene-7,8-dihydrodiol-9,10-epoxide (CHEBI:30614) is the ultimate carcinogenic metabolite of BaP oxidation — both consistent with a Phase I functionalization phenotype. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently recovers L-cysteine-driven hits in hsa00430 'Cysteine and methionine metabolism' (p=0.02) and hsa00770 'Nicotinate and nicotinamide metabolism' (p=0.049), reflecting the central role of cysteine as a glutathione precursor and as a cofactor for xenobiotic-conjugating enzymes. The convergent signal across ORA (RaMP) and m/z-network (Mummichog) methods, anchored by methimazole, coumarin, L-cysteine, and catechol, points to an upregulated Phase I oxidative xenobiotic metabolism phenotype in the treatment group, with benzo[a]pyrene-diol-epoxide presence confirming exposure to polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons.
